titleText.es: Probablemente los mejores abrazos los dan  los mixinos, que pueden extrudir filamentos microscópicos que convierten un gran volumen de agua en baba en cuestión de segundos. ¡Una manta blandita instantánea!
titleText.en: The best hugs are probably from hagfish, which can extrude microscopic filaments that convert a huge volume of water around them to slime in seconds. Instant cozy blanket!
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and official title attributes are preserved exactly, including the doubled space in dan  los. OCR split the two printed copies of CIENTÍFICOS, plus PROBLEMA, AUMENTADO, and ABRAZARTE, across line wraps; each remains one lexical occurrence. OCR also restored TÍO, JA, LA before the taxonomic label, and QUIERE. F. SEPTICA is an audited scientific-name exclusion.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here científicos is a plural noun naming people who do science, not an adjective meaning “scientific.”
Quitáis is the present form used with informal plural vosotros, common in Spain.
Analizar stays in its unchanged dictionary form, and las attaches to represent the feminine plural things being analyzed.

example.es: Necesito analizar las muestras; voy a analizarlas mañana.
example.en: I need to analyze the samples; I am going to analyze them tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In slime molds, plasmodios are the creeping, multinucleate stages of the organism.

example.es: Los plasmodios se desplazan hacia el alimento.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mucilaginoso literally means slimy or mucilaginous. In moho mucilaginoso it forms the conventional Spanish name for a slime mold.
After a form of haber, aumentado is aumentar’s completed-action form.
Resistentes is plural to match the things that have this resistance.

example.es: Estas plantas son resistentes al frío.
example.en: These plants are resistant to cold.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ja represents a short burst of laughter in writing.
Mola is an informal expression common in Spain for saying that something is cool or appealing.
Olvida is the positive informal command for one listener, and lo attaches for the thing to forget. The written accent keeps the original stress.

example.en: If it does not work, forget it.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Veis is the present form of ver for informal plural vosotros, common in Spain.

example.en: Do you all see that light?

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks the person or thing in which a quality is perceived
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In verle una cualidad a alguien o algo, le marks one person or thing and les marks more than one. It appears before a changed form of ver or attaches to ver in its unchanged dictionary form. Natural English usually expresses the same relation with ‘in.’

example.en: I see a future in the project.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: in; introduces the person or thing in which a quality is perceived
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After verle una cualidad, a can introduce or clarify the person or thing associated with that quality. Natural English usually rearranges the idea and uses ‘in.’

example.es: Le veo un defecto al plan.
example.en: I see a flaw in the plan.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks moverse, “to move”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With mueve, se shows that the organism itself moves.
Mueve is the present form of mover for one person or thing. With se, it means that thing moves itself.
Quiere is the present form of querer for one person or thing. Before another verb in its dictionary form, it expresses what that subject wants to do.
Abrazar stays in its unchanged dictionary form, and te attaches for one familiar person being hugged.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce the situation that is causing a problem?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: El problema names the difficulty, es identifies it, and que introduces the situation that follows. A de phrase may be inserted after problema to say whose problem it is.

example.es: El problema es que no tenemos tiempo.
example.en: The problem is that we do not have time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the Spanish term for “slime mold”?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Moho means mold and mucilaginoso means slimy, but together they are the conventional Spanish name for a slime mold, a group of amoeba-like organisms rather than ordinary fungus.

example.es: El moho mucilaginoso vive en lugares húmedos.
example.en: Slime mold lives in damp places.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something makes a person or thing become a certain way?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of hacer, then the affected person or thing, then the word that describes the resulting quality.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hacer changes for the person and time. The affected person or thing can be a noun or a short object word such as me, te, lo, la, los, or las. The final describing word agrees with what it describes: resistente becomes resistentes for a plural object.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: verle una cualidad a alguien o algo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that you see a quality in someone or something?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of ver with le or les, name the quality, and optionally clarify the person or thing with a.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ver changes for the person and time: for example, veo, ves, or veis. With a changed form, put le for one entity or les for more than one before the verb. Name the perceived quality next; a can then introduce the person or thing explicitly. Natural English usually rearranges this as ‘see a quality in someone or something.’

example.es: Le veo mucho potencial a esta idea.
example.en: I see a lot of potential in this idea.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: moho mucilaginoso · vómito de perro · abrazo
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The characters admire a slime mold until its dog-vomit nickname and autonomous movement make the encounter grotesquely affectionate.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The organism is discussed with genuine scientific enthusiasm and claims about pigment and zinc resistance. The joke repeatedly collides that analytical wonder with its appearance, its crude nickname, and the final suggestion that the moving blob wants a hug.
